subject: CAN
body: Canada is a constitutional monarchy, a parliamentary democracy and a
explanation: Three key facts about Canada's system of government.

subject: CAN
body: Who is Canada's Head of State?
explanation: The Governor General represents the Sovereign in Canada.

subject: CAN
body: Who represents the Sovereign in Canada?
explanation: Lieutenant Governors represent the Sovereign in the provinces.

subject: CAN
body: Who is the head of the federal government?
explanation: The PM selects Cabinet ministers.

subject: CAN
body: What are the three parts of Parliament?
options: The PM, the Cabinet and the courts
The Sovereign, the Senate and the House of Commons
The House, the Senate and the Supreme Court
explanation: Bills must pass both Houses and receive Royal Assent.

subject: CAN
body: Members of the House of Commons are called
explanation: They are elected in federal elections.

subject: CAN
body: How are senators chosen?
options: Appointed by the Governor General on the advice of the Prime Minister
explanation: They serve until age 75.

subject: CAN
body: What is the head of a provincial government called?
explanation: Territories also have premiers.

subject: CAN
body: How many provinces and territories does Canada have?
explanation: Territories: Yukon, Northwest Territories and Nunavut.

subject: CAN
body: What is the minimum voting age in federal elections?
explanation: Voters must be Canadian citizens.

subject: CAN
body: Elections are held using which system?
options: First past the post — the candidate with the most votes wins
explanation: Each riding elects one MP.

subject: CAN
body: In what year was the Canadian Charter of Rights and Freedoms entrenched in the Constitution?
explanation: Part of the Constitution Act, 1982.

subject: CAN
body: Which of these is a responsibility of citizenship?
options: Serving on a jury when called
explanation: Others include voting, obeying the law and helping others.

subject: CAN
body: What are Canada's two official languages?
explanation: Protected by the Official Languages Act.

subject: CAN
body: Which right is protected by the Charter?
options: Mobility rights — to live and work anywhere in Canada
explanation: Also freedom of expression, religion and peaceful assembly.

subject: CAN
body: In what year did Canada become a country (Confederation)?
explanation: July 1, 1867 — now Canada Day.

subject: CAN
body: Which four provinces joined Confederation first?
options: Quebec, Nova Scotia, PEI and Newfoundland
Ontario, Quebec, Nova Scotia and New Brunswick
explanation: The Fathers of Confederation created the Dominion of Canada.

subject: CAN
body: Who was Canada's first Prime Minister?
explanation: He served from 1867.

subject: CAN
body: Who was the first French-Canadian Prime Minister since Confederation?
explanation: His portrait is on the $5 bill.

subject: CAN
body: What were the Aboriginal peoples of Canada called collectively in the Constitution?
explanation: Three distinct groups.

subject: CAN
body: What is the Battle of Vimy Ridge (1917) remembered for?
options: A Second World War naval battle
A defining Canadian victory in the First World War
explanation: Over 10,000 Canadians were killed or wounded.

subject: CAN
body: What did the Canadian Pacific Railway, completed in 1885, do?
options: Connected Canada to the USA only
Linked Canada from coast to coast
explanation: It helped unite the country.

subject: CAN
body: When is Remembrance Day?
explanation: Canadians wear the poppy to honour those who served.

subject: CAN
body: What is the capital of Canada?
explanation: Located in Ontario.

subject: CAN
body: What is the capital of Quebec?
explanation: Montreal is the largest city in Quebec.

subject: CAN
body: What is the capital of British Columbia?
explanation: On Vancouver Island.

subject: CAN
body: What is the capital of Alberta?
explanation: Calgary is Alberta's largest city.

subject: CAN
body: What is the capital of Nova Scotia?
explanation: A major Atlantic port.

subject: CAN
body: What is the capital of Nunavut?
explanation: Nunavut was created in 1999.

subject: CAN
body: Which ocean borders Canada to the north?
explanation: Canada's motto refers to 'from sea to sea'.

subject: CAN
body: Which is Canada's most populous province?
explanation: More than a third of Canadians live in Ontario.

subject: CAN
body: What is on the Canadian flag?
explanation: Adopted in 1965.

subject: CAN
body: What is the national anthem of Canada?
explanation: Proclaimed the national anthem in 1980.

subject: CAN
body: What is Canada's motto?
options: From sea to sea (A mari usque ad mare)
explanation: 'Peace, order and good government' is from the Constitution.
